name: Inkspira
tagline: Small German AI writing tool sold on subscription tiers, aimed at people who need drafts out the door faster than they can type them.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Anything that is fundamentally an editor plus a library of prompt templates plus a model call is weekend territory, and this looks like that shape. An agent can give you a local workspace with projects, a markdown editor, saved prompts, streaming rewrites and version history in one sitting. The gaps are the boring ones: you bring your own API key, you pay per token, and nobody tuned the prompts for your language or your genre except you. We also have not verified the full feature list or the price, so treat this as a shape judgment rather than a feature-by-feature teardown. If the product turns out to lean on fine-tuned models or a proprietary corpus, the verdict drops.
coreLoopDIY: A local writing workspace where you keep documents, hit one of your own saved prompt templates, and get a streamed rewrite or expansion you can accept, diff or discard.
requirements: An OpenAI-compatible API key, billed per token
Willingness to write your own prompt templates instead of inheriting someone else's
whatYouLose: Prompt templates someone else already tested on thousands of documents, including German-language quirks
Hosted sync, so your drafts live on one machine unless you wire up storage yourself
Any mobile or tablet writing surface
Per-token cost predictability: a flat subscription hides a lot of model spend
Onboarding, polish and the small UX decisions that make a writing tool pleasant instead of a form with a textarea
moatNotes: Writing tools live or die on feel. The model is commodity, the prompt library and the editor ergonomics are the product.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a subscription is a flat number and token billing is not, and because most people do not want to maintain a text editor as a side project. A paid tool arrives with prompts that were already iterated on, a UI that does not fight you at 11pm, and the quiet promise that someone will fix it when the model vendor changes an endpoint. The DIY build wins on control and loses on the fact that you now own every rough edge.
notes: We could not confirm the pricing tiers or the full feature set, so this entry judges the category shape rather than the specific product.
prompt:
Build a local-only AI writing workspace. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable: Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, SQLite via better-sqlite3. Single process, runs with `npm run dev` on localhost. No auth, no Docker, no ORM beyond raw SQL in a thin db module.

Data model: projects (id, title, created_at), documents (id, project_id, title, body_markdown, updated_at), revisions (id, document_id, body_markdown, source, created_at), templates (id, name, system_prompt, user_prompt_with_placeholders).

Features that are in scope:
- Sidebar with projects and documents, create, rename, delete, all local.
- Markdown editor: plain textarea with monospace font, autosave to SQLite on a 1 second debounce. Do not install a rich text editor.
- Template runner: pick a saved template, choose selection or whole document as input, send to the model, stream the result into a right-hand panel.
- Accept, replace selection, append, or discard. Every accept writes a row to revisions.
- Revision list per document with a plain unified diff view against the current body.
- Seed six starter templates: outline, expand, tighten, change tone, continue in the same voice, summarise. Keep the prompts short and editable in the UI.
- Export a document as .md, export a project as a zip of .md files.

Out of scope, do not build: collaboration, sharing links, image generation, payments, mobile layouts, onboarding tours, chat history.

Model calls: OpenAI-compatible chat completions with streaming, base URL and key from .env (OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_BASE_URL, MODEL). Server-side route handler only, never expose the key to the client. If the key is missing, render a clear banner instead of crashing.

Ship a README with setup in five lines, a note that the SQLite file is the only state, and a warning that every generation costs tokens.
